historical_commentary.text: This note is a fascinating time capsule from the height of the MP3 revolution (1999, the Napster era). Building an MP3 jukebox within a database application was cutting-edge and showed 4D's versatility beyond traditional business applications. The ID3 tag reading/writing capability demonstrated useful metadata handling. Today, media playback would be handled through system APIs or web-based players, and music databases are ubiquitous (iTunes/Apple Music debuted in 2001). The specific techniques are obsolete, but the concept of database-driven media management was prescient.
related_updates: Modern 4D can interact with media through system commands or Web Areas
ID3 tag libraries are now available as standard open-source components
Streaming services have largely replaced local MP3 jukebox applications
